conventions.convention: A phase domain is a nonempty open subset of R^(2n), n ≥ 1, with grouped coordinate order (q,p), λ = Σ p_i dq^i, ω = −dλ = Σ dq^i ∧ dp_i, and J = [[0,I],[-I,0]].

Finite-regularity forms and pullbacks are coordinate, pointwise objects. A C^r canonical map preserves ω; a canonical transformation additionally is a C^r diffeomorphism. X_h = J∇h for C² h, with contraction convention ι_Xh ω = dh. The coordinate bracket extends to C¹ inputs; C² inputs yield a C¹ bracket, without closure of C² under brackets.
Generating functions are C³ with nonzero mixed determinant. First kind uses p = S_q and P = −S_Q; second kind uses p = S_q and Q = S_P. Generated maps are local C² maps.
The time-dependent first-kind convention gives K = H + ∂_t S and p dq − H dt = P dQ − K dt + dS, with all terms evaluated on the declared (t,q,Q) domain.

A Hamilton–Jacobi complete integral is C³, solves S_t + H(t,q,S_q) = 0, and has invertible S_qα at the specified base point. Its momentum is p = S_q and its Jacobi constants are β = S_α; canonical labels have order (β,α).

Hamiltonian evolution conclusions hold on actual maximal existence domains. Nonautonomous evolution has separate initial and final times, and the inverse exchanges those endpoints; completeness is not assumed.

Phase-volume preservation retains Countable Choice for the cited Lebesgue change-of-variables theorem. The main statement uses bounded Borel sets whose closures lie in the evolution domain; the Remarks separately justify extension to all Lebesgue-measurable sets, including infinite measure.

Action-angle coordinates use period-one angles in R^n/Z^n and ω = Σ dθ_i ∧ dI_i. Their existence assumes Countable Choice, a nonempty compact connected regular fibre, and a saturated proper-submersion neighbourhood with connected fibres. The original base neighbourhood B₀ and action-coordinate ball A are distinct coordinate images.
Radian rescaling means the quotient diffeomorphism [x] ↦ [2πx] from R/Z to R/(2πZ), together with I_rad = I/(2π); it preserves ω and multiplies cyclic frequencies by 2π.

load_bearing.statement: A phase domain is a nonempty open U ⊆ R^(2n), n ≥ 1, with λ_U = Σ p_i dq^i, ω_U = Σ dq^i ∧ dp_i = −dλ_U, and J = [[0,I],[-I,0]].
Defines finite-regularity coordinate forms, pointwise pullbacks, C^r canonical maps and transformations, X_h = J∇h for C² h, and the coordinate bracket ∇fᵀJ∇g for C¹ inputs.

For C¹ C:U→V between phase domains, C*ω_V = ω_U iff DCᵀJDC = J everywhere. A canonical C¹ diffeomorphism has |det DC| = 1. For a canonical C² diffeomorphism and H ∈ C²(V), DC(z)X_(H∘C)(z) = X_H(C(z)).

For a C² autonomous Hamiltonian, Y(t) = D_zΦ_t(z₀) is C¹ on the maximal lifetime and satisfies Y′ = J Hess H(Φ_t(z₀))Y, Y(0) = I, YᵀJY = J, and det Y = 1. The corresponding assertions hold for jointly C² nonautonomous Hamiltonians and their two-time evolution, whose domain is open and whose fixed-endpoint maps have reverse-endpoint inverses.
For either kind of generating-function data in the preceding definition, the generated map C is a canonical C² local diffeomorphism and |det DC| = 1 wherever defined.

A C³ complete integral for a C² Hamiltonian produces local Hamilton characteristics with p = S_q, constant β = S_α, a local converse solving β = S_α for q, and local canonical labels satisfying dq ∧ dp = dβ ∧ dα at fixed time.

Under Countable Choice, complete integrability, a nonempty compact connected regular fibre, and a saturated proper-submersion neighbourhood over regular values with connected fibres, there are a base neighbourhood B₀ and action-coordinate ball A giving period-one action-angle coordinates on U₀ = π⁻¹(B₀), with ω = Σ dθ_i ∧ dI_i; every smooth fibre-constant function depends only on I.
For a smooth closed two-form τ on an open set star-shaped about 0, α_x(v) = ∫₀¹ t τ_tx(x,v) dt is a smooth one-form with dα = τ.

concerns.concern: The Definition says the cited inverse-function theorem makes Ψ a 'local C² diffeomorphism'. The opened thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem states only a C¹ inverse. The C² upgrade is valid but needs the short derivative-formula argument: Dg = (DΨ∘g)⁻¹ is C¹, hence g is C². The same attribution occurs in generating-function and Hamilton–Jacobi consumers; outside pthm-cm13-generating-functions F2 already writes this upgrade explicitly.

The Statement requires W″ to be an open ball. Proof 1.1 obtains only an open inverse-function neighbourhood W″, whereas step 3.1 immediately says 'The ball W″ is open and star-shaped'. Insert the missing restriction to a ball inside the inverse-function image, replacing W by its inverse image. This preserves the claim.

The first bullet says 'AC_ω enters only in the counterexample sequence of step 4.1'. The opened compact-flow corollary, lattice lemma, and torus theorem explicitly require inherited Countable Choice as well. The local theorem assumes it correctly; the scope prose should distinguish its direct step-4.1 use from inherited supplier assumptions.

alerts.finding: Published proof step 5.2 says 'On the ball [F4] gives τ=dα' for τ = σ*ω, a closed two-form. F4 cites thm-poincare-lemma-for-star-shaped-domains, whose opened Statement concerns closed C¹ vector fields and scalar potentials, equivalently one-forms. It does not supply a primitive of a two-form. The batch's separate k = 2 lemma repairs its own local theorem, but the published carrier still has this unsupported citation.

F2 writes 'X_h=J∇h=(-h_ϑ,h_I)' and cites the batch's fixed J = [[0,I],[-I,0]], defined in (q,p) = (ϑ,I) order. The KAM phase maps use (I,ϑ) order. In that order the displayed component formula is correct, but its matrix is −J. For h(I,ϑ)=I₁, the cited J applied to the action-first gradient gives (0,−e₁), whereas the claimed field is (0,e₁). No permuted J is defined in this F2. The owning group should resolve the matrix/order mismatch.

F3 writes 'X_f=J∇f=(-f_ϑ,f_I)' while the Statement explicitly takes the field in action-angle order (p,ϑ). The cited phase-domain J is defined in angle-first order. With the action-first gradient, f=p₁ gives J∇f=(0,−e₁), not (0,e₁). The component formula and translation test can remain valid after an explicit coordinate permutation, but the matrix equality as written is false.

The Hamiltonian paragraph says 'the Hamiltonian vector field of a C¹ Hamiltonian H is, by prop-cm-hamiltonian-field-and-poisson-bracket-in-a-phase-chart' the displayed coordinate field. That supplier assumes C² H and concludes a C¹ field; the local finite-calculus definition also defines X_h for C² h. The C¹ extension is mathematically immediate as a continuous field satisfying the contraction identity, but should be identified as a local definition/derivation rather than attributed to the stronger-regularity supplier. Actual holomorphic Hamiltonian data have adequate regularity.

Complete-integral and characteristics citations preserve C²/C³ regularity and local invertibility. Checked the harmonic example's cited action-angle and radian formulas and companion page scope. Its positive-action punctured-plane chart and rescaling agree with the supplier; no existence across oscillator caustics is attributed to the local Hamilton–Jacobi theorem.

Complexification is explicitly defined locally rather than inferred from a real-only supplier. Drift/kick/Verlet consumers faithfully use the real matrix criterion and finite C² canonical terminology, separating algebraic composition domains from flow segment-containment conditions.

The pulsed-oscillator definition uses the same (q,p), ω and Hamiltonian-field signs. The pulse-map item explicitly proves time-dependent symplecticity locally rather than relying on an autonomous-only assertion.

The KAM definition correctly pairs (q,p)=(ϑ,I), then states the action-first component order separately. Two later F-blocks nevertheless write X=J∇ using the unchanged angle-first J with action-first components; exact counterchecks are recorded in alerts. The definition also attributes a C¹ extension to a C² supplier.
